Title: RV quick-save accepts non-finite numbers
Reproduction Steps: POST /api/cases/{id}/rv with raw application/json body {"rows":[{"issuer":"A","instrument":"B","currency":"USD","price":Infinity}]} - JSON carries the Infinity/NaN literals and Python's json.loads accepts them.
Expected Result: 422 - invariant 7 refuses non-finite values before use, exactly as contracts.RVRow.finite_number does for the other RV row model.
Actual Result: 201. The value is stored as float('inf') and serialized back to the analyst as null, so the number silently disappears. store.py builds its engine with json_serializer=json.dumps (allow_nan defaults True), so the rv_universes JSON column receives a literal Infinity - invalid JSON that a Postgres json/jsonb column refuses outright, which is what production runs.
Root Cause: api/__init__.py::RVQuickRow is a second, hand-rolled twin of contracts.RVRow written without the finite_or_none validators the original carries. Pydantic v2 admits inf/nan into a float field by default and renders them as null on JSON serialization, so nothing downstream complained.
Fix: Added a finite_number validator over price/yield_bps/spread_bps/duration on RVQuickRow, reusing contracts.finite_or_none.

Title: Control characters accepted in pinned text
Reproduction Steps: POST /api/cases with raw body {"name":"a\u0007b","issuer":"I","sector":"S"}; likewise POST .../notes with {"body":"a\u0007b"} and an RV row issuer.
Expected Result: 422 - CLAUDE.md's standing boundary rule: every string that can enter pinned state or events must UTF-8-encode, reject lone surrogates and be NFC-normalized at the API boundary.
Actual Result: 201, and the control byte is persisted in the case row, the note body and the RV universe, and rides into the audit event.
Root Cause: contracts.validate_boundary_text existed but was wired to exactly one field - StartRunRequest.focus_questions. Case identity, note bodies and RV row text all reach pinned state and audit events with no boundary check at all.
Fix: Lifted validate_boundary_text above the models and added BoundaryText = Annotated[str, AfterValidator(validate_boundary_text)]; applied it to CreateCaseRequest.name/issuer/sector, NoteRequest.body and RVQuickRow.issuer/instrument.

Title: Issuer identity not NFC-normalized
Reproduction Steps: POST /api/cases twice with the same issuer spelled NFD (Cafe + combining acute) and NFC (precomposed e-acute).
Expected Result: Both normalize to one issuer string, so one issuer cannot mint two lineages - the boundary rule requires NFC before any pin is computed.
Actual Result: Two cases whose issuer strings compare unequal despite rendering identically; every downstream digest, snapshot and deliverable identity forks.
Root Cause: Same root cause as D-002: NFC folding lives inside validate_boundary_text, which was never applied to case identity.
Fix: Covered by the same BoundaryText change; the regression test asserts the two spellings round-trip to one value.

Title: Pathway fit is computed but never served
Reproduction Steps: Create a case, upload a source, GET /api/cases/{id} and read pathway_fit. Then open /cases/ in the workbench.
Expected Result: The Cases screen's Pathway fit panel shows READY or a warning with a message - what sources.domain.pathway_fit computes and what the frontend CaseRecord type and panel already render.
Actual Result: pathway_fit is absent from every case response, so the panel permanently reads 'Fit unavailable. Pathway fit is not served by this deployment.' The backend helper is live and unit-tested (test_source_ingestion.py:88 asserts fit == READY) but no route calls it.
Root Cause: _wire_case adds source_count and the deep-research flags but never calls sources.domain.pathway_fit, and CaseResponse does not declare the field. The frontend comment shows the absence was known; whether to close it is a product decision.
Fix: Wired it, following the repo's own documented procedure for a wire change (CLAUDE.md): a new CasePathwayFitResponse serving only the two fields the frontend declares (fit, message), pathway_fit added to CaseResponse, _wire_case calling sources.domain.pathway_fit, and the pinned key set in test_http_contracts_spec.py updated. The now-stale frontend comment claiming the wire serves no such field was corrected. This is wire-visible and easy to revert if it was a deliberate omission.

Title: NFC normalization ran after the length bound
Reproduction Steps: POST /api/cases with a name of 160 x U+0958 (DEVANAGARI KA WITH NUKTA, a Unicode composition exclusion that folds to two code points under NFC).
Expected Result: 422 string_too_long - min_length/max_length must bound the value that actually gets stored.
Actual Result: 201, with a 320-character name persisted in a field declared max_length=160. The same 2x amplification applied to issuer (160), sector (120), note body (12000) and focus questions (400).
Root Cause: Self-inflicted by the D-002/D-003 fix: BoundaryText was built on AfterValidator, which pydantic runs after the str constraints, so the bound was checked on the pre-normalized value and the transform then grew it. The pre-existing StartRunRequest.boundary_clean_questions field_validator had the identical ordering bug.
Fix: Rebuilt BoundaryText on BeforeValidator with a non-str passthrough (so `name: 123` still fails as string_type rather than crashing in the validator), and replaced the focus-questions field_validator with the same annotated item type so its ordering is fixed too.
Regression Test: caos/tests/spec/test_state_spec.py::test_case_and_note_text_is_boundary_validated_at_the_api_contract (asserts 160 expanding chars are refused and 80 store as exactly 160)

Title: Dead agent kill switches in operator-facing config
Reproduction Steps: Read caos/.env.example lines 37-40 and the app/worker environment blocks of caos/deploy/docker-compose.yml, then grep the codebase for those names.
Expected Result: Every environment variable an operator is shown is one the application actually reads. AGENT_EXECUTION_ENABLED is the documented fail-closed switch.
Actual Result: CPDR_AGENT_ENABLED, CANONICAL_AGENT_ENABLED, CPDR_PILOT_CASE_IDS and CPDR_PILOT_SUBJECTS are set on both services and documented in .env.example, but Settings.from_env reads none of them and no other code references them. CANONICAL_AGENT_ENABLED=false sits directly beside AGENT_EXECUTION_ENABLED=false, so an operator can believe they have disabled canonical agent execution while it is fully enabled - a fail-open misreading of the one flag the design calls fail-closed.
Root Cause: Legacy carryover from the pre-LangGraph deployment. Nothing removed them when Settings.from_env was rewritten to a single agent flag, and no test asserts that every compose variable is read.
Fix: Deleted the four dead entries from docker-compose.yml (app and worker) and from .env.example. Pure deletion - nothing reads them.
Regression Test: Re-ran the full nightly deployment step locally: compose --no-interpolate, compose with a filled env, verify_image_resources.py and check_module_consistency.py all pass.

Title: Nightly deployment job has been failing every night
Reproduction Steps: gh run list --workflow=nightly.yml -> the last three runs all FAIL; the failing job is 'Nightly - deployment and methodology checks'. Reproduced locally: docker compose --env-file caos/.env.example -f caos/deploy/docker-compose.yml config -q.
Expected Result: The nightly deployment job runs its four checks and passes.
Actual Result: The step's second command fails with 'required variable SESSION_SECRET is missing a value'. Under `shell: /usr/bin/bash -e` the step aborts there, so python caos/deploy/verify_image_resources.py and check_module_consistency.py NEVER RUN. Confirmed in the run 33307788675 log. Both checks pass when run by hand, so the failure has been masking two working gates rather than a real defect.
Root Cause: .env.example deliberately ships every required secret EMPTY so Compose's ${VAR:?} fails closed - ci.yml carries a six-line comment explaining that the file therefore cannot be fed to `config` as-is, and fills the blanks with sed first. nightly.yml was never given that treatment and runs the exact command ci.yml documents as impossible.
Fix: Mirrored ci.yml's fill-then-validate in nightly.yml, keeping the check's real purpose (a variable MISSING from the example still fails, an intentionally empty value does not).
Regression Test: Whole step reproduced locally end to end: all four commands pass. Also verified the ci.yml required-secrets-ship-empty check still passes after the .env.example edit.

Title: No guard tied the edge header scrub to the headers the app trusts
Reproduction Steps: grep the test suite for Caddyfile or oauth2-proxy: nothing references either. Then delete the `request_header -X-Forwarded-Groups` line from caos/deploy/Caddyfile and run the suite - before this session it stayed green.
Expected Result: A test fails when an identity header the app trusts is not stripped from the client request at the edge.
Actual Result: Nothing checked. The auth edge is two files that must agree - Caddy strips X-Forwarded-User/Email/Groups and X-Edge-Authorization so identity_from_request can trust them - and adding a trusted header to identity.py without adding a scrub line would let a client inject it straight through. That is an auth bypass produced by editing one file, with no test standing in the way.
Root Cause: Latent, not live: today the two lists agree for every header that matters, and x-caos-role is deliberately outside the scrub set because production never reads it. The defect is the missing guard, not a current bypass.
Fix: Added a test that derives BOTH sets from source (regex over the Caddyfile and over identity.py) and asserts the production-trusted set is a subset of the scrubbed set, so drift is what fails rather than a stale restatement. Added a behavioural twin asserting x-caos-role cannot escalate in production even if it does reach the app.

Title: test:production-inventory targets routes this build does not serve
Reproduction Steps: CAOS_URL=... CAOS_EDGE_SECRET=... npm run test:production-inventory against a production-mode instance.
Expected Result: The advertised npm script runs and reports the deployment inventory.
Actual Result: It aborts at line 256. The script walks GET /api/cases/{id}/runs (only POST is served here -> 404 confirmed live) and /api/cases/{id}/members (no route at all -> 404 confirmed live), and CAOS_CASE_ID defaults to a fixture id case_d5e3151a64554296 from a seeded environment expecting an issuer named Synthetic Dense Issuer with 100+ sources. It cannot pass against this build in any configuration.
Root Cause: Written against a different (seeded, fuller) deployment and never reconciled with the route set this server actually serves. It is not wired into CI, so nothing surfaced the drift.
Fix: Not deleted - it is a real inventory for a deployment that serves those routes. Added a header comment on the script stating exactly which routes are missing and that it is not a check on this build, and an entry in the CLAUDE.md known-gaps ledger, which is the repo's own mechanism for this.
Regression Test: Confirmed live against a production-mode instance on :8012: both routes answer 404.

Title: The CI Python SAST gate can pass while scanning nothing
Reproduction Steps: Run the security job's bandit command under Python 3.14: bandit -r caos/server/caos -x .../vendor --severity-level high --confidence-level medium; echo $?.
Expected Result: A SAST gate either scans the code or fails.
Actual Result: bandit 1.7.10 raises 'Constant object has no attribute s' on every server file (it reaches for the ast.Constant.s alias a newer interpreter dropped), SKIPS all 35 of them, reports 0 issues and EXITS 0. A passing gate and a gate that scanned nothing are indistinguishable. Verified both ways: on Python 3.12, 9621 lines scanned and 0 files skipped; on 3.14, 0 lines scanned and exit 0.
Root Cause: Latent, not live: CI pins python-version 3.12 in the security job, so the gate works today. The defect is that the pin is undocumented and load-bearing - bumping it to match the 3.14 leg of the server matrix would silently disable SAST.
Fix: Rewrote the Python SAST step to emit bandit's JSON report and assert on it: no parse errors, and at least 5000 lines covered. Verified by executing the exact step body extracted from ci.yml - exit 0 on 3.12, exit 1 on 3.14 with the parse-error message. Comment records why the interpreter pin matters.

Title: BeforeValidator let bytes bypass the boundary check
Reproduction Steps: CreateCaseRequest(name=b'a\x07b', issuer='I') in process, or any in-process caller passing bytes to a BoundaryText field.
Expected Result: Refused - the boundary rule is the last line before pinned state and must not depend on the caller's chosen input type.
Actual Result: ACCEPTED, storing 'a\x07b'. bytes carrying an NFD form were also accepted unnormalized. The AfterValidator form this replaced refused the identical input.
Root Cause: Self-inflicted by the D-005 fix. Moving to BeforeValidator to get the ordering right meant the validator now sees the RAW input, and the isinstance(value, str) guard only covered one of the shapes pydantic accepts as a string - lax mode decodes bytes to str AFTER the validator has already waved them through. Not reachable over the JSON wire; reachable from the engine, worker, tests and any future internal caller.
Fix: _boundary_before now decodes bytes/bytearray as UTF-8 and validates the result, letting an undecodable value fall through to the str schema (string_unicode) rather than raising from inside the validator. Everything else still passes through untouched, so name=123 remains string_type.
Regression Test: caos/tests/spec/test_state_spec.py::test_case_and_note_text_is_boundary_validated_at_the_api_contract (bytes clause; verified red with the bytes branch removed)

Title: pathway_fit loaded every evidence block on the case-list route
Reproduction Steps: Seed 20 cases x 3 sources x 300 blocks x 2000 chars, then time GET /api/cases.
Expected Result: A signal derived from filename suffixes costs about what reading the filenames costs.
Actual Result: 100 ms for a 9,571-byte response; 92 of those 100 ms were pathway_fit. It called store.list_sources, which selects the whole source row including the blocks JSON column - 1.8 MB of block text for one case with three modest sources, 3.9 ms per case against 0.10 ms for the read beside it. The cost scaled with evidence volume, not case count, on the route the frontend refetches after every run event.
Root Cause: Self-inflicted when wiring D-004. list_sources was the obvious call and its name says nothing about the blocks column riding along. I wrote a longer comment about the existing N+1 instead of measuring the read I was adding.
Fix: Added DomainStore.list_source_filenames - one narrow SELECT of the filename column for live sources - and pointed pathway_fit at it. GET /api/cases went 100 ms -> 19 ms on the same fixture, and the cost no longer tracks evidence volume.
Regression Test: caos/tests/test_source_ingestion.py::test_pathway_fit_never_reads_the_blocks_column (stubs list_sources to raise; verified red against the old call)

Title: Capacity harness job drivers died on the application's own 429s
Reproduction Steps: Run `qa/capacity.py profile` at the declared profile (25 subjects, 20 jobs, 4 streams, 300 rpm) against the candidate stack; count `Traceback` lines in the log after four minutes.
Expected Result: The application refuses above-ceiling requests with a typed 429 and the harness backs off and keeps its twenty job slots occupied for the whole soak.
Actual Result: Every job driver thread died within four minutes (`RuntimeError: run … unreadable for this subject: 429`, then `httpx.ReadTimeout`): `wait_terminal` re-raised on any non-run body and `job_driver` caught nothing, so the soak degraded to readers only while still writing a profile.
Root Cause: The harness treated every non-200 as fatal; the 300/min per-subject bucket is exactly what the profile drives at, so the first refusal on a poll was inevitable. Found on candidate 2026-09-03-c4f0270 (soak attempts 1 and 2, retained).
Fix: `admitted()` retries a 429 or a transport error with a capped backoff until a deadline; `drive_once` records every failure under `driver_error` with its class and the driver thread never dies; `wait_terminal` polls through `admitted`.

Title: Capacity harness stream holders spun on a closed stream and drained the subject's bucket
Reproduction Steps: Same profile run; read `stream_open` counts in `samples.jsonl` (6,203 opens in three minutes for 100 holders) and the sampler's traceback.
Expected Result: Four sustained event streams per subject, one open per holder per window.
Actual Result: Once a case's run was terminal the events tail closed immediately and the holder reopened it in a tight loop, spending the subject's whole 300/min bucket; the sampler's `leakage_check` then indexed a 429 body (`TypeError: string indices must be integers`) and died, so resource samples stopped.
Root Cause: No pause between a closed stream and the next open, and a listing parsed without checking it was a list.
Fix: The holder holds one stream per 30 s window and waits out the rest of the window; `foreign_cases` returns None for a non-list body and the sampler records it as `refused` instead of crashing.
Regression Test: caos/tests/test_capacity_harness.py::test_foreign_cases_ignores_a_refused_listing (red before the fix); the holder's window is exercised by the candidate soak

Title: Capacity harness seeded 21 distinct documents per case, not 100
Reproduction Steps: Same profile run; read the seed phase's `upload` statuses in `samples.jsonl`.
Actual Result: `upload 10000 → 201: 2100, 409: 7900`: `text_document` varied only the line count (`12 + document % 20`), so 79 of every 100 seed uploads were byte-identical duplicates the application refused with 409.
Root Cause: The seed document was keyed by case and line count only.
Fix: `seed_document(case_index, document)` puts the document index into the text, so every seeded document of a case is distinct.

Title: Workbench smoke failed under WebKit on a slow runner for fetches WebKit rejects at navigation
Reproduction Steps: Run `CAOS_BROWSER=webkit node scripts/workbench-smoke.mjs` on a slow runner (CI run 33863698677, twice), or locally with responses held ~2 s via page.route while navigating between routes.
Expected Result: The journey completes and the report lists no page errors; a genuine cross-origin or blocked request still fails the run.
Actual Result: Five, then nine page errors of the form `/127.0.0.1:8000/<route> due to access control checks.` for Next's segment-cache prefetch GETs and HEAD route probes; the retained trace shows every one of those URLs answered 200 same-origin and 11 requests aborted at navigation.
Root Cause: WebKit rejects a same-origin fetch still in flight when the document navigates with a TypeError worded as an access-control failure (Chromium and Firefox never settle those promises); Next's prefetches are unawaited, so the rejection surfaces as an unhandled-rejection page error, which the smoke recorded verbatim. Local runs never left a prefetch in flight (FCP ~130 ms vs 1 669 ms on the runner).
Fix: `scripts/webkit-teardown.mjs::webkitTeardownRejection` drops such a page error only under WebKit, only for a URL same-origin with the server under test, and only with evidence the server was not refusing it: the page saw that exact URL answered 2xx/3xx by a non-document request, or the request was abandoned without any response while the same path had been answered 2xx/3xx earlier on the page (a prefetch's `_rsc` query changes per navigation); every dropped entry is retained in `workbench-report.json::webkit_teardown_rejections`. The smoke's three remaining instant focus-return reads (palette trigger, compile control, accept-dialog cancel) now wait for the frame the workspace restores focus on, like every other site since Task 12b (CI run 33875704963 lost that race on the compile control).
Regression Test: caos/frontend/scripts/webkit-teardown.test.mjs (7 tests, red before the module existed; run by `npm run test:unit`); the held-response reproduction dropped 2 of 2 with evidence and kept a synthetic cross-origin one
